Withdraw a bad build, in production and test at once: no app is served it again, whether through a
location's showing, rules or pins or an experiment arm. Each of those serves the most recent earlier
build deployed there that is not withdrawn and fits the location instead, an arm preferring the
builds it kept before, or no paywall when there is none. Apps that cannot show a newer build are
never given it either.

Nothing deployed or placed changes. The build cannot be deployed until 'voidhash paywall restore'
restores it; to put a fixed design in front of people, deploy it afterwards with 'voidhash paywall
deploy'.

Lists each place that serves the build and what it serves instead, then asks; --yes skips that.

Usage:
  voidhash paywall withdraw [paywall] [flags]

Arguments:
  paywall  The paywall's slug, name or id

Flags:
      --build <number>     The build, by number or id
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
  -y, --yes                Make the change without asking for confirmation

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash paywall withdraw pro --build 4
  voidhash paywall withdraw pro --build 4 --yes
